Coffee is one of the most widely consumed beverages in the world. Its ______ can be traced back to the ancient coffee forests on the Ethiopian plateau.
questions.explanation: The sentence discusses the beginning or historical start of coffee. The word 'origins' perfectly fits to mean the point or place where something begins, arises, or is derived.

Legend says that a goat ______ named Kaldi first discovered the potential of these beloved beans.
questions.explanation: A person who looks after a herd of livestock or makes a living from keeping them is called a 'herder'. A 'goat herder' is the correct historical and contextual term.

He noticed that after eating the berries from a certain tree, his goats became so ______ that they did not want to sleep at night.
questions.explanation: Because the goats 'did not want to sleep at night', they must have been full of energy. 'Energetic' is the only logical choice that fits the context of caffeine consumption.

Kaldi reported his findings to the ______ of the local monastery...
questions.explanation: A monastery is governed by an 'abbot' (a man who is the head of an abbey of monks). The other options are civil or secular roles that do not belong in a monastery.

The abbot shared his discovery with the other monks, and knowledge of the energizing berries began to ______.
questions.explanation: When knowledge is shared among people, it 'spreads'. The other words (vanish, shrink, perish) imply a decrease or destruction, which contradicts the context of sharing a popular discovery.

questions.explanation: Since it is grown 'in a multitude of countries around the world', the resulting commodity is 'massive global'. 'Local', 'restricted', or 'regional' contradict the worldwide scope described in the sentence.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and fill in blank (1).

Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest _____(1)_____ dance forms of India, traces its origins to Tamil Nadu. Originally _____(2)_____ in temples by devadasis, it was later revived and brought to the concert stage. The dance is _____(3)_____ for its intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and sculptural poses. Each movement _____(4)_____ a specific emotion or narrative drawn from Hindu mythology. Its three _____(5)_____ components — Nritta, Nritya, and Natya — represent pure movement, expressive dance, and drama respectively. The theoretical _____(6)_____ of Bharatanatyam is the Natya Shastra, attributed to Bharata Muni. The expressive aspect, known as _____(7)_____, involves conveying emotions through facial expressions, gestures, and eye movements.
questions.explanation: 'Classical' is the correct term — Bharatanatyam is one of eight dance forms recognized as classical by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, implying formal codification and a scriptural theoretical tradition. 'Ancestral' and 'primitive' describe antiquity but lack the implication of structured, codified pedagogy that defines a classical art.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and fill in blank (2).

Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest _____(1)_____ dance forms of India, traces its origins to Tamil Nadu. Originally _____(2)_____ in temples by devadasis, it was later revived and brought to the concert stage. The dance is _____(3)_____ for its intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and sculptural poses. Each movement _____(4)_____ a specific emotion or narrative drawn from Hindu mythology. Its three _____(5)_____ components — Nritta, Nritya, and Natya — represent pure movement, expressive dance, and drama respectively. The theoretical _____(6)_____ of Bharatanatyam is the Natya Shastra, attributed to Bharata Muni. The expressive aspect, known as _____(7)_____, involves conveying emotions through facial expressions, gestures, and eye movements.
questions.explanation: 'Performed' correctly describes devadasis who danced sacred rituals as an offering to the deity — the action is one of enactment, not veneration. 'Worshipped' implies the devadasis themselves were the object of reverence, reversing the subject-object relationship. 'Scripted' and 'celebrated' do not collocate naturally with temple dance practice.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and fill in blank (3).

Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest _____(1)_____ dance forms of India, traces its origins to Tamil Nadu. Originally _____(2)_____ in temples by devadasis, it was later revived and brought to the concert stage. The dance is _____(3)_____ for its intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and sculptural poses. Each movement _____(4)_____ a specific emotion or narrative drawn from Hindu mythology. Its three _____(5)_____ components — Nritta, Nritya, and Natya — represent pure movement, expressive dance, and drama respectively. The theoretical _____(6)_____ of Bharatanatyam is the Natya Shastra, attributed to Bharata Muni. The expressive aspect, known as _____(7)_____, involves conveying emotions through facial expressions, gestures, and eye movements.
questions.explanation: 'Renowned' (widely known and admired) is the idiomatic collocate for 'renowned for its features' in formal descriptive writing. 'Acclaimed' is the most tempting distractor — it implies praise but is used for one-time recognition events (an acclaimed film), whereas 'renowned' denotes enduring, widespread repute. 'Notorious' implies infamy and is semantically opposite.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and fill in blank (4).

Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest _____(1)_____ dance forms of India, traces its origins to Tamil Nadu. Originally _____(2)_____ in temples by devadasis, it was later revived and brought to the concert stage. The dance is _____(3)_____ for its intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and sculptural poses. Each movement _____(4)_____ a specific emotion or narrative drawn from Hindu mythology. Its three _____(5)_____ components — Nritta, Nritya, and Natya — represent pure movement, expressive dance, and drama respectively. The theoretical _____(6)_____ of Bharatanatyam is the Natya Shastra, attributed to Bharata Muni. The expressive aspect, known as _____(7)_____, involves conveying emotions through facial expressions, gestures, and eye movements.
questions.explanation: 'Conveys' means to communicate or transmit — each Bharatanatyam movement is purposefully designed to express (convey) a bhava or mythological narrative to the audience. 'Conceals' is the direct antonym and a classic vocabulary trap. 'Disrupts' implies interference with meaning, and 'ignores' implies indifference — both contradict the intentional communicative design of the dance.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and fill in blank (5).

Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest _____(1)_____ dance forms of India, traces its origins to Tamil Nadu. Originally _____(2)_____ in temples by devadasis, it was later revived and brought to the concert stage. The dance is _____(3)_____ for its intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and sculptural poses. Each movement _____(4)_____ a specific emotion or narrative drawn from Hindu mythology. Its three _____(5)_____ components — Nritta, Nritya, and Natya — represent pure movement, expressive dance, and drama respectively. The theoretical _____(6)_____ of Bharatanatyam is the Natya Shastra, attributed to Bharata Muni. The expressive aspect, known as _____(7)_____, involves conveying emotions through facial expressions, gestures, and eye movements.
questions.explanation: 'Distinct' correctly describes the three components because Nritta (pure technical movement with no narrative), Nritya (movement fused with expression), and Natya (dramatic storytelling) are fundamentally different in intent and execution. 'Similar' is factually incorrect — conflating these three would misrepresent the structure of the art form. 'Confusing' and 'repeated' carry negative connotations absent from the passage.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and fill in blank (6).

Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest _____(1)_____ dance forms of India, traces its origins to Tamil Nadu. Originally _____(2)_____ in temples by devadasis, it was later revived and brought to the concert stage. The dance is _____(3)_____ for its intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and sculptural poses. Each movement _____(4)_____ a specific emotion or narrative drawn from Hindu mythology. Its three _____(5)_____ components — Nritta, Nritya, and Natya — represent pure movement, expressive dance, and drama respectively. The theoretical _____(6)_____ of Bharatanatyam is the Natya Shastra, attributed to Bharata Muni. The expressive aspect, known as _____(7)_____, involves conveying emotions through facial expressions, gestures, and eye movements.
questions.explanation: 'Foundation' correctly identifies the Natya Shastra as the theoretical basis (structural grounding) upon which Bharatanatyam and all Indian classical arts are built. This requires knowing that the Natya Shastra is a prescriptive treatise, not a commentary or critique — which eliminates 'criticism'. 'Weakness' is semantically opposite. 'Disruption' implies the text undermined rather than established the tradition.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and fill in blank (7).

Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest _____(1)_____ dance forms of India, traces its origins to Tamil Nadu. Originally _____(2)_____ in temples by devadasis, it was later revived and brought to the concert stage. The dance is _____(3)_____ for its intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and sculptural poses. Each movement _____(4)_____ a specific emotion or narrative drawn from Hindu mythology. Its three _____(5)_____ components — Nritta, Nritya, and Natya — represent pure movement, expressive dance, and drama respectively. The theoretical _____(6)_____ of Bharatanatyam is the Natya Shastra, attributed to Bharata Muni. The expressive aspect, known as _____(7)_____, involves conveying emotions through facial expressions, gestures, and eye movements.
questions.explanation: 'Abhinaya' is the Sanskrit technical term for the expressive-communicative dimension of Bharatanatyam, encompassing Sattvika (inner emotion), Angika (body language), and Vachika (vocal elements). 'Thandava' is the vigorous masculine dance style attributed to Shiva — a style category, not an expressive technique. 'Mangalam' is the auspicious closing item of a recital. 'Alamkara' refers to melodic ornaments in Indian music, not dance expression.
